question: Should Claws become a core lifecycle owner for installing and removing globally shared `mcp.servers` entries, despite the existing bundle-plugin MCP path?
rationale: The patch is gated and technically repairable, but it creates durable core authority over executable and remote capability while VISION.md prefers bundle-style plugin ownership and the governing RFC remains open.

options.title: Defer pending RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open until the RFC and prerequisite stack explicitly approve the core ownership boundary, then require the redaction fix and real lifecycle proof.

options.title: Approve core ownership
options.body: Accept the new owner after the URL-redaction defect, coexistence rules, upgrade behavior, recovery contract, and real proof are complete.

options.title: Use bundle ownership
options.body: Move package-driven MCP declarations into the existing compatible bundle/plugin lifecycle and avoid adding another core ownership ledger.

recommendation.title: Defer pending RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open until the RFC and prerequisite stack explicitly approve the core ownership boundary, then require the redaction fix and real lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the strongest merged history for the current MCP registry and bundle runtime boundary affected by this decision.
